expectations.text: The response rejects the claim that charging a fee is cheaper to run than free childcare, stating the subsidized model carries more organizer effort (fee handling and administration), and wins only when the budget line rather than organizer hours is the binding constraint.
expectations.evidence: 'Charging adds work: payment handling, refunds, no-shows'; 'right answer only when the budget line is what binds, not organizer hours (skill: Menu 4)'.

expectations.text: It states that any published fee filters out exactly the families the program exists to reach, which is why a subsidized fee sits last on value.
expectations.evidence: '"any fee filters out the families the program was for."'

expectations.text: It treats the dozen parents in last edition's feedback as the documented evidence that promotes on-site childcare - provisioning against evidence held rather than a template.
expectations.evidence: 'A dozen parents told you they couldn't attend without childcare. That is your evidence of need (Q3).'

expectations.text: It rejects the volunteer parent as the caregiver, requiring vetted standards: caregivers certified and experienced in childcare, police-background-verified, and insured.
expectations.evidence: Qualifications, 'police or public-safety clearance', 'first-aid and CPR certification, plus insurance'; 'One volunteer fails the two-carer minimum'.

expectations.text: It cites child-to-caregiver ratios by age band - 1:2 for 0-11 months, 1:3 for 1-3 years, 1:6 for 4-12 years - as questions to put to a vendor.
expectations.evidence: 'PyCon: 1:2 for 0–11 months, 1:3 for 1–3 years, 1:6 for 4–12 years.'

expectations.text: It labels those ratios as one vendor's published standard to compare against, not a regulatory minimum, since jurisdictional requirements vary and belong with counsel.
expectations.evidence: 'reused as questions to ask, not as law'; Portugal requirements go to counsel.

expectations.text: It states that placing minors in the event's care is the heaviest and least reversible review on any menu, since an incident cannot be undone.
expectations.evidence: 'Minors in your care is the least reversible commitment in the whole skill.'

expectations.text: It confirms the entity requirement is satisfiable here (a registered non-profit) and requires the contract, insurance, and a named organizer owning the vendor relationship before committing.
expectations.evidence: 'A non-profit is a legal entity, so Q4 is fine. You can sign a vendor contract and carry insurance'; volunteer as named owner; 'Replace the volunteer plan with a vetted vendor'.

expectations.text: It states that if the vetting, insurance, or entity requirement cannot be met, the provision is unavailable and must be said so, never run in a reduced version.
expectations.evidence: 'the skill says the provision isn't available. Don't run a reduced version.'

expectations.text: It separates the nursing room from childcare as a distinct provision and rejects merging the two rooms.
expectations.evidence: 'Don't merge it into the childcare room'; 'A merged room fails both jobs.'

expectations.text: It recommends publishing the nursing room's existence unconditionally (location may be withheld until check-in) over hiding its existence behind a contact request, because the first reaches people who would never ask.
expectations.evidence: 'Publish it unconditionally. State that it exists and withhold only the location until check-in.'

expectations.text: It requires an RSVP mechanic with capacity and register-early framing for the childcare provision rather than open drop-in.
expectations.evidence: 'It needs booking, so use RSVP with a named owner'; page entry 'capacity N, RSVP by <date>'; 'Cap the capacity from RSVP numbers'.

expectations.text: If the subsidized route is kept, it carries the sourced cost pattern as a ratio - the published fee sits well below the real per-child-day cost, roughly a quarter of it - not as a currency figure to copy.
expectations.evidence: 'the real cost per child-day was about four times the fee... Transpose the ratio, not the currency.'
